log: LOOP 236 -- MORE MATCHED EXPERIMENTS, AND A SIGN PREDICTED BEFORE LOOKING
Our target is dexamethasone ADDED. GSE144662 measures dexamethasone TAKEN AWAY.
If both read the same programme, the correlation must be NEGATIVE. The sign is the
test, and noise has no sign.
GSE304966 was found and is UNUSABLE: its counts matrix has 36 header fields, 36 data
fields and a numeric first field, so it carries no gene identifiers.

U7 DOES A CONSENSUS BEAT sci-PLEX ALONE?
sci-Plex dose series alone 0.7474 +/- 0.0012
consensus of all three      0.9281 +/- 0.0003
PAIRED +0.1807 +/- 0.0002  (+789.8 standard errors)
loop 235 measured sci-Plex alone at 0.7709 on its own gene set
U7 PASS -- the consensus gains +0.1807 at 789.8 standard errors; averaging independent experiments helps as loop 232's law predicts
U8 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Every arm here is a MEASUREMENT of the outcome, not a prediction of it. A consensus
reaching 0.85 would mean the response is highly reproducible across laboratories,
not that we can model it. Loop 235 S4 already measured what the curated biology adds
on top of one such measurement: +0.0081.
The blocker arms differ from the dex arm in more than GR occupancy -- mifepristone
and CORT113176 have off-target effects and KH-103 removes a protein used elsewhere.
A collapse under blockade is consistent with GR-dependence without isolating it.
GSE144662's washout starts after 12 h of dex, so its 00h is a fully induced state.
It measures decay of an established response, and slow-turnover genes will look
least affected however strongly they responded.
